g.text: Name:
Date:
OCT
The Universal Postal Union is founded
What clue would you check first on October 9?
Have you ever wondered how a calendar date can open a big story? On
October 9, The Universal Postal Union was founded on October 9, 1874,
and that anniversary is remembered as World Post Day. This story focuses
on one memorable detail from The Universal Postal Union is founded. The
class checks Universal Postal Union before treating a date or name as a
fact. Then students use a friendly classroom model connected to the
topic. The numbers 7, 9, 8, 25, 15, 1874, 1.5, 150 appear in today's
three math tasks; they are practice quantities unless the passage
clearly identifies them as historical measurements. That difference
matters: history tells us what happened, while a worksheet gives us a
fair way to practice arithmetic. Look for the challenge, mistake,
invention, animal, or celebration in the story. Ask which detail came
from the source and which number was added for practice. Read the title
aloud, circle useful clues, and explain how the math grows from the same
topic. Level 1 uses one direct addition or subtraction step. Level 2
uses multiplication or division. Level 3 combines steps, units, time,
money, or a comparison. A careful history detective checks both the
story and the answer before sharing the result.
